title: Jeremiah Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah
Judah mourneth
Their nobles have sent their little ones
The ground is chapt
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Jeremiah 14:1.

questions.question: What is the condition of Judah as described in Jeremiah 14:2?
options: They are rejoicing
They mourneth
They are thriving
They are at peace
questions.correctAnswer: They mourneth
questions.explanation: Judah is described as mourning in Jeremiah 14:2.

questions.question: What did the nobles send their little ones to find in Jeremiah 14:3?
options: Food
Water
Grass
Shelter
questions.correctAnswer: Water
questions.explanation: The nobles sent their little ones to the waters to find water, as stated in Jeremiah 14:3.

questions.question: What did the little ones find when they went to the pits in Jeremiah 14:3?
options: Plenty of water
No water
Some food
Fresh grass
questions.correctAnswer: No water
questions.explanation: They found no water when they returned with their vessels empty, as mentioned in Jeremiah 14:3.

questions.question: Why were the plowmen ashamed in Jeremiah 14:4?
options: Because they were lazy
Because the ground is chapt
Because they lost their tools
Because they were attacked
questions.correctAnswer: Because the ground is chapt
questions.explanation: The plowmen were ashamed because the ground is chapt due to a lack of rain, as stated in Jeremiah 14:4.

questions.question: What happened to the hind in the field according to Jeremiah 14:5?
options: It stayed with its young
It calved and forsook it
It found food
It ran away
questions.correctAnswer: It calved and forsook it
questions.explanation: The hind calved in the field and forsook it because there was no grass, as stated in Jeremiah 14:5.

questions.question: What did the wild asses do in the high places according to Jeremiah 14:6?
options: They grazed peacefully
They snuffed up the wind
They ran away
They rested
questions.correctAnswer: They snuffed up the wind
questions.explanation: The wild asses stood in high places and snuffed up the wind like dragons, as mentioned in Jeremiah 14:6.

questions.question: What do the iniquities testify against according to Jeremiah 14:7?
options: The people
The land
The leaders
The nations
questions.correctAnswer: The people
questions.explanation: The verse states that our iniquities testify against us, referring to the people, as seen in Jeremiah 14:7.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 14:8, who is referred to as the hope of Israel?
options: Jeremiah
The LORD
The king
The prophets
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: The verse refers to the hope of Israel as the LORD, indicating His role as savior in times of trouble, as stated in Jeremiah 14:8.

questions.question: What is the state of Jerusalem's gates in Jeremiah 14:2?
options: They are open
They are locked
They languish
They are bustling
questions.correctAnswer: They languish
questions.explanation: The gates of Jerusalem are described as languishing in Jeremiah 14:2.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 14:4, why did the ground become chapt?
options: Too many plowmen
No rain in the earth
It was overwatered
It was too dry
questions.correctAnswer: No rain in the earth
questions.explanation: The ground is chapt because there was no rain in the earth, as stated in Jeremiah 14:4.

questions.question: True or False: The cry of Jerusalem is gone up according to Jeremiah 14:2.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text states that the cry of Jerusalem has gone up, confirming the statement in Jeremiah 14:2.

questions.question: True or False: The wild asses had plenty of grass as per Jeremiah 14:6.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text indicates that the wild asses' eyes failed because there was no grass, confirming the statement in Jeremiah 14:6.

questions.question: True or False: The hind stayed with its young in the field according to Jeremiah 14:5.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text states that the hind forsook its young because there was no grass, contradicting the statement.

questions.question: True or False: The nobles of Judah sent their elders to find water according to Jeremiah 14:3.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text specifically states that the nobles sent their little ones, not elders, to find water.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 14:9, why should the LORD not be as a man astonied or a mighty man that cannot save?
options: Because the LORD is in the midst of us and we are called by His name
Because the people have forsaken Him
Because He has abandoned Jerusalem
Because no one calls upon His name
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD is in the midst of us and we are called by His name
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:9 says, 'yet thou, O LORD, art in the midst of us, and we are called by thy name; leave us not.' This explains why the LORD should not be as a man astonied or unable to save.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 14:11 promise will happen if one prays for the people’s good, as commanded in Jeremiah 14:10?
options: The LORD will not hear their prayer
The LORD will accept their offerings
The LORD will send rain upon the land
The LORD will forgive their sins
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will not hear their prayer
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:10 commands about the people's wandering and sin, and Jeremiah 14:11 says, 'Then said the LORD unto me, Pray not for this people for their good,' indicating prayers will not be heard.

questions.question: What consequence does the LORD declare in Jeremiah 14:12 for when the people fast and offer burnt offerings?
options: He will not hear their cry and will consume them by sword, famine, and pestilence
He will accept their offerings and bring peace
He will forgive their sins and restore the land
He will send prophets to guide them
questions.correctAnswer: He will not hear their cry and will consume them by sword, famine, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:12 states that when they fast and offer burnt offerings, the LORD will not accept them but will consume them by sword, famine, and pestilence.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 14:13 and 14:14 contrast the messages of the true LORD and the false prophets?
options: The false prophets promise peace, but the LORD says they prophesy lies and false visions
The LORD promises peace, and the false prophets warn of sword and famine
Both the LORD and the false prophets promise peace and prosperity
The false prophets are silent, but the LORD commands war
questions.correctAnswer: The false prophets promise peace, but the LORD says they prophesy lies and false visions
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:13 shows prophets saying there will be peace, but Jeremiah 14:14 reveals these prophets prophesy lies and false visions in the LORD’s name.

questions.question: What reason does the LORD give in Jeremiah 14:10 for not accepting the people?
options: They have loved to wander and have not refrained their feet
They have built altars to false gods
They have not fasted sincerely
They have not offered sufficient sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: They have loved to wander and have not refrained their feet
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:10 states, 'Thus have they loved to wander, they have not refrained their feet, therefore the LORD doth not accept them.'

questions.question: What does Jeremiah express in Jeremiah 14:13 about the prophets’ message compared to the LORD’s warning?
options: The prophets say there will be no sword or famine and will give assured peace
The prophets warn of sword and famine coming soon
The prophets tell the people to repent and fast sincerely
The prophets remain silent in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: The prophets say there will be no sword or famine and will give assured peace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:13 says, 'the prophets say unto them, Ye shall not see the sword, neither shall ye have famine; but I will give you assured peace in this place.'

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 14:15, what will happen to the false prophets who declare there will be no sword or famine?
options: They shall be consumed by sword and famine
They will be exalted among the people
They will be forgiven for their deception
They will lead the people into peace
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be consumed by sword and famine
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:15 says, 'By sword and famine shall those prophets be consumed,' referring to false prophets who deny the coming judgment.

questions.question: What fate does the LORD declare for the people who listen to the false prophets, according to Jeremiah 14:16?
options: They shall be cast out in the streets and have none to bury them
They shall be protected from famine and sword
They shall be restored to their land
They shall receive abundant rain
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cast out in the streets and have none to bury them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:16 declares that the people will be cast out in the streets and have no one to bury them because of famine and sword.

questions.question: Why does Jeremiah call upon the LORD in Jeremiah 14:7 despite the people's many sins?
options: For the LORD’s name’s sake and because He is the hope of Israel
Because the people have repented fully
Because the false prophets have convinced him
Because the land is fertile again
questions.correctAnswer: For the LORD’s name’s sake and because He is the hope of Israel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:7 says, 'O LORD, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name's sake,' indicating Jeremiah appeals to God's reputation and role as hope.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 14:8, what metaphor is used to describe the LORD’s seeming absence or delay in helping Israel?
options: As a stranger in the land and a wayfaring man that turneth aside to tarry for a night
As a mighty warrior who fights for his people
As a shepherd leading his flock
As a king sitting on his throne
questions.correctAnswer: As a stranger in the land and a wayfaring man that turneth aside to tarry for a night
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:8 refers to the LORD as 'a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man that turneth aside to tarry for a night,' expressing Israel’s feeling of abandonment.

questions.question: What natural calamity is described in Jeremiah 14:4 as affecting the land and the plowmen?
options: No rain causing the ground to be parched
Flood waters covering the fields
Strong winds destroying the crops
Earthquakes shaking the land
questions.correctAnswer: No rain causing the ground to be parched
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:4 states, 'Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the plowmen were ashamed, they covered their heads.'

questions.question: How do the wild asses react to the lack of grass according to Jeremiah 14:6?
options: They stand in the high places, snuff up the wind like dragons, and their eyes fail
They flee to the rivers seeking water
They gather in herds to search for food
They lie down quietly in the fields
questions.correctAnswer: They stand in the high places, snuff up the wind like dragons, and their eyes fail
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:6 describes the wild asses standing in high places, snuffing the wind like dragons, and their eyes failing for lack of grass.

questions.question: What is the LORD’s attitude toward the people's fasting and offerings as stated in Jeremiah 14:12?
options: He will not hear their cry nor accept their burnt offerings and oblations
He will accept them and bless the land
He will require more sacrifices
He will send rain to the earth
questions.correctAnswer: He will not hear their cry nor accept their burnt offerings and oblations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:12 says, 'When they fast, I will not hear their cry; and when they offer burnt offering and an oblation, I will not accept them.'

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 14:7 shows Jeremiah asking the LORD to act because the people have not sinned and are blameless.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:7 acknowledges the people's many sins and iniquities, so Jeremiah asks the LORD to act for His name's sake despite their guilt.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 14:14 states that the LORD sent the prophets who prophesy peace and assured safety to the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:14 explicitly says the LORD did not send these prophets; they prophesy lies and false visions in His name.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 14.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 14:17, what is the reason given for the prophet's continuous weeping day and night?
options: The virgin daughter of my people is broken with a great breach, with a very grievous blow
The land is desolate and without water
The priests and prophets wander in a foreign land
The enemies have taken the city by force
questions.correctAnswer: The virgin daughter of my people is broken with a great breach, with a very grievous blow
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:17 states that the prophet's eyes shall run down with tears because 'the virgin daughter of my people is broken with a great breach, with a very grievous blow'.

questions.question: What is observed when Jeremiah goes into the field and the city as described in Jeremiah 14:18?
options: Slain with the sword in the field and sick with famine in the city
Cities burning and fields overgrown with thorns
Priests and prophets teaching in the temple
Enemies gathering to attack Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Slain with the sword in the field and sick with famine in the city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:18 describes seeing the slain with the sword in the field and those sick with famine in the city.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 14:19, what lament does the speaker express about Judah and Zion?
options: Hast thou utterly rejected Judah? hath thy soul lothed Zion?
The enemies have surrounded the city and the walls are broken
Our crops have failed and the wells are dry
The priests have forsaken the altar
questions.correctAnswer: Hast thou utterly rejected Judah? hath thy soul lothed Zion?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 contains the lament, 'Hast thou utterly rejected Judah? hath thy soul lothed Zion?' expressing a feeling of divine rejection.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 14:20, what do the people acknowledge?
options: Our wickedness, and the iniquity of our fathers: for we have sinned against thee
The destruction of the city is our deserved punishment
The false prophets have misled us
The famine is a test of our faith
questions.correctAnswer: Our wickedness, and the iniquity of our fathers: for we have sinned against thee
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:20 explicitly states the acknowledgment of wickedness and sin against God.

questions.question: What plea is made to God in Jeremiah 14:21?
options: Do not abhor us, for thy name's sake, do not disgrace the throne of thy glory
Send rain upon the earth to end the famine
Let the sword pass from us
Raise up a deliverer from among the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Do not abhor us, for thy name's sake, do not disgrace the throne of thy glory
questions.explanation: Verse 21 contains the plea not to be abhorred or disgraced for God's name's sake.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 14:22, why will the people wait upon the LORD?
options: Because thou hast made all these things
Because the Gentiles have failed to send rain
Because the heavens refuse to give showers
Because the priests have instructed them to do so
questions.correctAnswer: Because thou hast made all these things
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:22 affirms waiting upon the LORD as He is the maker of all things and the true source of rain and showers.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'betulah' (בתולה) in Jeremiah 14:17 mean?
options: Virgin
Widow
Daughter
Bride
questions.correctAnswer: Virgin
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'betulah' in Jeremiah 14:17 means 'virgin,' symbolizing purity and often personifying Jerusalem or Israel as the virgin daughter of the people.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Jeremiah 14:18 where the prophet contrasts the slain in the field and the hungry in the city?
options: Parallelism
Chiasm
Metaphor
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:18 uses parallelism by juxtaposing two related images — the slain with the sword in the field and the sick with famine in the city — to emphasize widespread devastation.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of divine rejection and lament found in Jeremiah 14:19?
options: Psalm 88:15
Genesis 1:1
Exodus 20:1
Proverbs 3:5
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 88:15
questions.explanation: Psalm 88:15 contains a similar lament questioning God's rejection and the absence of healing, paralleling the themes in Jeremiah 14:19.

questions.question: Jeremiah 14:20's confession of sin parallels which New Testament passage emphasizing repentance?
options: 1 John 1:9
Matthew 5:9
Romans 8:28
Hebrews 11:1
questions.correctAnswer: 1 John 1:9
questions.explanation: 1 John 1:9 stresses confession and forgiveness of sins, paralleling the confession of sin in Jeremiah 14:20.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Jeremiah 14:17 in the chapter?
options: The LORD's judgment on false prophets
A call to fasting and prayer
A description of famine and drought
An instruction to build altars
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD's judgment on false prophets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:14-16 describe the LORD's condemnation of false prophets, which immediately precedes the lament in 14:17.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 14:22, the rhetorical question about rain challenges the power of Gentile idols. What does this imply about Israel's understanding of God?
options: Only the LORD can control nature and provide rain
Idols are stronger than the LORD
Rain is unpredictable and comes from multiple sources
The Gentiles have a special relationship with the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: Only the LORD can control nature and provide rain
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:22 asserts that no Gentile vanity can cause rain, only the LORD, emphasizing monotheistic belief in God's sovereignty over nature.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Jeremiah 14:17 where the 'virgin daughter' imagery is used to describe Jerusalem?
options: Personification
Simile
Hyperbole
Paradox
questions.correctAnswer: Personification
questions.explanation: The 'virgin daughter' in Jeremiah 14:17 is personification, attributing human qualities to Jerusalem as a pure young woman suffering grievously.

questions.question: Jeremiah 14:18 mentions both 'the prophet and the priest go about into a land that they know not.' What historical event does this likely foreshadow?
options: The Babylonian exile
The Egyptian captivity
The Assyrian invasion
The Roman conquest
questions.correctAnswer: The Babylonian exile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:18 foreshadows the Babylonian exile where priests and prophets were taken to a foreign land unknown to them.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 14:21 appeals to God to remember and not break the covenant with His people for His own name's sake.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:21 explicitly petitions God not to break His covenant for the sake of His name and glory.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 14:7 teach about God's nature in relation to human sin?
options: God acts solely on human merit without regard to His name
God’s actions are motivated by His own name’s sake despite human iniquity
God ignores human sin because of His mercy
God’s justice requires immediate punishment without intercession
questions.correctAnswer: God’s actions are motivated by His own name’s sake despite human iniquity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:7 states, 'O LORD, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name's sake,' showing that God’s actions are influenced by His own name’s honor despite human sinfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in Jeremiah 14:10?
options: God accepts repentance without remembering sins
God will remember iniquity and visit sins due to persistent rebellion
God’s judgment is arbitrary and unpredictable
God’s forgiveness negates all consequences of sin
questions.correctAnswer: God will remember iniquity and visit sins due to persistent rebellion
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:10 says, 'he will now remember their iniquity, and visit their sins,' indicating that persistent rebellion leads to divine judgment remembering sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about false prophecy does Jeremiah 14:14 teach?
options: False prophets always speak with God’s permission
False prophets prophesy lies without God’s command or sending
False prophecy is a legitimate form of divine revelation
God endorses all prophetic messages regardless of content
questions.correctAnswer: False prophets prophesy lies without God’s command or sending
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:14 states, 'The prophets prophesy lies in my name: I sent them not, neither have I commanded them,' clarifying that false prophets act without divine authorization.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 14:12 specifically demonstrate?
options: Omnipotence
Justice
Omniscience
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:12 highlights God’s refusal to hear fasting and sacrifices and His intent to consume by sword, famine, and pestilence, demonstrating His attribute of justice in punishing sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 14:21 specifically demonstrate?
options: Covenant Faithfulness
Wrath
Omnipresence
Transcendence
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:21 says, 'remember, break not thy covenant with us,' emphasizing God's attribute of covenant faithfulness despite Israel's sin.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 14:17 prepare for the theme of divine lamentation found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It introduces God's joyful celebration of His people
It exemplifies divine sorrow over human sin and suffering
It depicts God's indifference to human pain
It denies any emotional response from God
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies divine sorrow over human sin and suffering
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:17 commands the prophet to let God's eyes run down with tears, showing divine lamentation similar to expressions of sorrow found in passages like Isaiah 63:9.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Jeremiah 14:8 establish concerning God’s presence with His people?
options: God is portrayed as a distant stranger
God is the hope and savior in times of trouble
God abandons His people permanently
God acts only through human effort
questions.correctAnswer: God is the hope and savior in times of trouble
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:8 calls God 'the hope of Israel, the saviour thereof in time of trouble,' linking to the broader biblical theme of God’s saving presence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 14:11 and 14:12 teach about prayer and fasting?
options: God always answers prayers regardless of people’s behavior
God refuses to listen to prayers and fasting when people persist in sin
Prayer and fasting guarantee divine acceptance without repentance
God’s silence means He is unaware of human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God refuses to listen to prayers and fasting when people persist in sin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:11 commands not to pray for the people’s good, and 14:12 explains that God will not hear fasting or accept offerings due to their sinfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 14:15 and 14:16 teach about false prophets and their consequences?
options: False prophets will be honored and rewarded
False prophets will be consumed by the very judgments they deny
False prophets have no impact on the people
False prophets bring peace and security
questions.correctAnswer: False prophets will be consumed by the very judgments they deny
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:15 warns that prophets denying sword and famine will themselves be consumed by these, and 14:16 describes the people suffering judgment due to false prophecy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 14:18 and 14:19 teach about the consequences of sin for both leaders and people?
options: Both prophet and priest are secure and know their land well
Both prophet and priest suffer disorientation and the people experience devastation
Sin affects only the laity, not spiritual leaders
Judgment is limited to physical death without spiritual consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Both prophet and priest suffer disorientation and the people experience devastation
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:18 depicts prophets and priests wandering unknown lands due to calamity, and 14:19 expresses the people's lament over rejection and lack of healing.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Jeremiah 14:11-12 teaches God’s rejection is unconditional and without hope. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God completely abandons His people with no possibility of restoration
God refuses to hear prayers during persistent sin but elsewhere calls for repentance
God’s rejection is permanent and irreversible
God’s silence means He is unaware of people’s suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God refuses to hear prayers during persistent sin but elsewhere calls for repentance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:11-12 shows God’s refusal to hear prayers due to sinfulness, but the chapter also includes pleas for mercy and covenant remembrance, indicating hope beyond judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty is taught in Jeremiah 14:6?
options: God loses control over creation during drought
God sovereignly allows creation to suffer consequences of human sin
God is powerless in the face of natural disasters
God’s sovereignty is limited to human affairs only
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly allows creation to suffer consequences of human sin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:6 describes wild asses failing due to no grass, indicating God’s sovereign control over nature’s response to human sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 14:22 specifically demonstrate?
options: Omnipotence
Immanence
Creator
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Creator
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:22 asks rhetorically if any gods of the Gentiles can cause rain or showers, then affirms the LORD as Creator of all things, demonstrating His creative power.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 14:2 contribute to the narrative arc about judgment and desolation in Scripture?
options: It portrays an image of restoration and abundance
It depicts mourning and desolation indicating divine judgment
It emphasizes human strength and resilience
It focuses on military conquest alone
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts mourning and desolation indicating divine judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:2 describes Judah mourning and gates languishing, symbolizing divine judgment and desolation, themes common in prophetic literature.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 14:20 and 14:21 teach about repentance and God’s covenant?
options: Confession leads to God breaking His covenant
Acknowledgment of sin is paired with plea for covenant mercy
Repentance is unnecessary for covenant relationship
God’s covenant is conditional solely on human works
questions.correctAnswer: Acknowledgment of sin is paired with plea for covenant mercy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 14:20 confesses wickedness and sin, while 14:21 pleads with God not to break His covenant, linking repentance with covenantal mercy.
